Hi Sophie — sorry for the confusion and thanks for flagging it.

Short answer: yes, we can absolutely send an explicit .ics that pins the slot to Europe/Paris (CEST) to avoid calendar clients re-interpreting the timezone. Calendly sometimes relies on the invitee's browser timezone setting; some calendar apps then convert to the device timezone incorrectly when DST transitions are recent.

Workaround I can do now:
- I'll send a manual .ics from our EU-hosted account that specifies TZID=Europe/Paris and an explicit UTC offset for the DTSTART/DTEND.
- If you'd prefer to rebook, please use the Calendly timezone dropdown (top-right) to set "Europe/Paris" before selecting a slot — that fixes it for most customers.

I'll loop in internal folks to push the ICS and mark the meeting as on our EU cluster.

Thanks — talk soon,
Priyom
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Evelyn,

Sophie at MediSys booked a 15:00 CEST demo for 6 May via Calendly but the invite landed as 23:00 on her calendar. Seems to be DST conversion oddness. Can CS or ops send a manual calendar invite (attached .ics) that pins Europe/Paris and mark the meeting as hosted from our EU cluster? Important so the automated host selection doesn't route them to a US instance.

Notes for ops:
- Use TZID=Europe/Paris and include DTSTART:20260506T150000
- Add a 10-minute pre-call buffer to the calendar event and set the conference location to "Zoom (EU) — Redwood"
- Paste the hubspot meeting ID in the description (linked below)

If you want, we can also drop a short instruction in the Calendly confirmation: "If your device shows a different time, please verify the timezone selector at the top of the Calendly page and select Europe/Paris." But given recent DST churn I think manual ICS is the safest for now.

Thanks,
Priyom
